newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on delivery talk, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on delivery talk, exports.

text.p: CBOT wheat closed sharply lower, led by December, on talk that deliveries on that contract may be heavier than expected, traders said.
"There's talk of wheat deliveries and talk of business going elsewhere," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

He referred to floor talk that one million to two million bushels of wheat will be posted Friday for delivery on the December. Friday is first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT December contracts.
Ideas circulated that Cargill Inc would post the wheat for delivery, the traders said.
The market early Wednesday was poised for a lighter delivery scenario of one million bushels or less.

In late dealings, Cargill Inc sold two million bushels of March and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold one half million bushels of March, traders said. Refco Inc bear spread one half million bushels of March/December and fund were said to be sellers of the market on the modified close.
Traders also said the market while not shocked, was disappointed that the U.S. failed to land recent export deals.
Wheat closed 12-1/2 cents per bushel lower to two higher, with December down 12-1/2 at $4.00-1/2 a bushel.
Sri Lanka and Morocco bypassed the U.S. in their wheat purchases this week which pressured CBOT wheat futures, traders said.
"The U.S. isn't getting any of the business," Kucha said.
Exporters said Sri Lanka bought 50,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia and 50,000 tonnes from Argentina. Morocco bought 20,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina, exporters said.
Wheat rallied Monday, partly due to ideas the U.S. would land some of the business.
Trading was quiet before the U.S. Thanksgiving Day Holiday Thursday. Markets closed early Wednesday at 1210 CST and will close Friday at 1210 CST.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 19,187 traded Tuesday.
In wheat options, Smith Barney bought 200 July $3.50 puts at 23-1/2 cents and Tenco Inc sold 200 March $3.70 puts at nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,500 contracts, below the 2,866 traded Tuesday.
